newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas corn, sorghum, rice harvest advances.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas corn, sorghum, rice harvest advances.

text.p: Clear weather aided grain harvest in the week ended September 15, the Arkansas Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly update.

Seven days were suitable for fieldwork but drought conditions were affecting some areas. Dryness hurt soybeans in Faulkner County. Statewide, soil moisture was rated 46 percent adequate, 39 percent short and 15 percent very short.
High winds caused some rice fields to lodge in Craighead County. But rice harvested rose to 41 percent complete from 15 pct a week ago and compared to 40 pct last week, 33 average.
Rice was rated 75 pct ripe vs 77 last year, 68 avg.
Corn harvest 78 pct vs 58 w/a, 85 y/a, 76 avg.
Soybeans harvested 6 pct vs 4 w/a, 2 y/a, 2 avg.
Soybeans mature 13 pct vs 9 w/a, 4 y/a, 4 avg.
Soybeans dropping leaves 18 pct vs 11 y/a, 9 avg.
Sorghum harvested 55 pct vs 39 w/a, 57 y/a, 51 avg.
Sorghum mature 87 pct vs 88 y/a, 83 avg.
Cotton harvested 4 pct vs 1 w/a, nil y/a, 1 avg.
Cotton opening bolls 71 pct vs 64 w/a, 74 y/a, 53 avg.
Wheat planted 1 pct vs nil y/a, 1 avg.
